description: A dark, painterly medieval market street. In the foreground a hooded figure in ragged mail lies face-down in the dirt beside a wooden stall with bread loaves in crates; a dropped spear and a torn cloth lie nearby. Behind them, mounted knights in plate armour and dark capes ride through a town of half-timbered houses, with more armoured men and spears in the background. No visible text, frame or wounds.
reason: Could be this event, but nothing in the picture identifies Wat Tyler or the Smithfield parley. It reads as a generic medieval riot with mounted men and a fallen commoner. To make it clearly this event, show a single mounted royal party facing a rebel leader in an open London square, with a mayor's man striking him.
